sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，与商业、政治和文化领域的一些最具影响力的领袖进行现场对话，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上对精选采访进行现场直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Two years after facing calls to resign over a racist image, the Democratic governor of Virginia, Ralph Northam,
sentences.zh: 在因一张种族主义照片而面临辞职呼声两年后，弗吉尼亚州民主党州长拉尔夫·诺瑟姆，

sentences.en: has instead emerged as the most racially progressive leader in the state's history.
sentences.zh: 反而一跃成为该州历史上种族进步最显著的领导人。

sentences.en: Today, Sabrina Tabernese spoke with our colleague, Asted Herndon, about how that happened.
sentences.zh: 今天，萨布丽娜·塔伯内塞与我们的同事阿斯特德·赫恩登谈论了这一切是如何发生的。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月17日，星期四。

sentences.en: Tell me why you became interested in this story, in the story of Ralph Northam.
sentences.zh: 告诉我，你为什么会对这个故事感兴趣，对拉尔夫·诺瑟姆的故事感兴趣？

sentences.en: Well, in 2019, I was really looking at the state of Virginia and thinking, what in the world is going on?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在2019年，我真的在审视弗吉尼亚州的情况，心想：这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: All right, what is going on in Virginia?
sentences.zh: 好吧，弗吉尼亚到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: The state was thrown into chaos when it came out that Governor Ralph Northam wore blackface in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 当爆出州长拉尔夫·诺瑟姆在20世纪80年代曾将脸涂黑扮演黑人（blackface）的消息时，整个州陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: The governor, who it was discovered on his medical school yearbook page, had a really racist photograph.
sentences.zh: 人们发现这位州长的医学院毕业纪念册页面上，有一张非常具有种族主义色彩的照片。

sentences.en: The picture shows two people, you can see it right there, one in blackface and another in a Ku Klux Klan robe and hood.
sentences.zh: 照片显示有两个人，你就在那里可以看到，一个人把脸涂黑，另一个人穿着三K党的长袍和头套。

sentences.en: A man in blackface, then another man in a KKK costume.
sentences.zh: 一个把脸涂黑的男子，然后是另一个穿着三K党服饰的男子。

sentences.en: Just a short time ago, the governor admitting one of those men is him.
sentences.zh: 就在不久前，州长承认其中一名男子就是他本人。

sentences.en: And the governor said initially that it was him, then flip-flopped the next day and said he doesn't think it was him.
sentences.zh: 州长最初承认那是他，但第二天又改口说他认为那不是他。

sentences.en: I am not the person in that photo.
sentences.zh: 照片里的那个人不是我。

sentences.en: But he did wear blackface on another time.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在另一个时候把脸涂黑过。

sentences.en: That same year, I did participate in a dance contest in which I darkened my face as part of a Michael Jackson costume.
sentences.zh: 同年，我确实参加了一场舞蹈比赛，作为迈克尔·杰克逊造型的一部分，我把脸涂黑了。

sentences.en: And it was a lot of cause for him to resign.
sentences.zh: 这引发了要求他辞职的大量呼声。

sentences.en: I think he should resign immediately.
sentences.zh: 我认为他应该立刻辞职。

sentences.en: The governor should resign.
sentences.zh: 州长应该辞职。

sentences.en: I think he's shown himself sort of irreparably damaged in terms of his ability to govern.
sentences.zh: 我认为他在治理能力方面已经受到了某种程度的无可挽回的损害。

sentences.en: Can Governor Northam survive this?
sentences.zh: 诺瑟姆州长能挺过这一关吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: But then a whole bunch of other stuff happened in the state, too.
sentences.zh: 但随后，州里还发生了许多其他的事情。

sentences.en: Justin Fairfax, lieutenant governor, facing two accusations of sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 副州长贾斯汀·费尔法克斯面临两项性侵指控。

sentences.en: The person who would have been next in line if Ralph Northam had stepped down.
sentences.zh: 如果拉尔夫·诺瑟姆下台，他本该是下一任接替者。

sentences.en: The lieutenant governor, he was accused of sexual assault by two women in this period, though he denies those allegations.
sentences.zh: 这位副州长在此期间被两名女性指控性侵，尽管他否认了这些指控。

sentences.en: He's hanging in the job right now as well.
sentences.zh: 目前他也依然在职。

sentences.en: And then you had the attorney general, who would have been third in line, also a Democrat, voluntarily admit that he wore blackface at a party in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 接着是本该排名第三的州总检察长，他也是一名民主党人，主动承认自己在20世纪80年代的一次聚会上把脸涂黑过。

sentences.en: The state's top three lawmakers now facing separate scandals, although they're all interconnected.
sentences.zh: 该州最高的三位立法者现在都面临各自的丑闻，尽管它们盘根错节。

sentences.en: So I think my reaction, sitting in New York at the time, was what was in the water in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我当时身在纽约时的反应是，弗吉尼亚的水里到底下了什么药。

sentences.en: And more interestingly enough, how come all these people, all three of them, stayed in office?
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是，为什么所有人，这整整三个人，都留任了？

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: I remember that series of very strange news items starting with Northam thinking, what?
sentences.zh: 我记得从诺瑟姆开始的那系列非常奇怪的新闻，当时就在想：什么？

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: And I remember him saying he wasn't going to leave.
sentences.zh: 我记得他说过他不会离开。

sentences.en: And then it seemed like the story just kind of faded away, right?
sentences.zh: 然后感觉这个故事就像是慢慢淡出了视野，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, on the national level, it did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在全国层面确实如此。

sentences.en: You had a Democratic Party that was obviously in the middle of a presidential primary and the election of Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 当时民主党正处于总统初选和乔·拜登选举的漩涡中心。

sentences.en: And that was where the attention was on the national level.
sentences.zh: 全国的注意力都集中在那里。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think as part of covering that is also following what's happening in the states.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为作为报道的一部分，也需要关注各州正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I was seeing a Virginia that certainly looked differently than before the scandal.
sentences.zh: 我看到现在的弗吉尼亚，和丑闻发生前相比确实大不一样了。

sentences.en: In November of 2019, Democrats became the majority in both houses of the state legislature,
sentences.zh: 在2019年11月，民主党人赢得了州议会两院的多数席位，

sentences.en: giving them really expanded political possibilities in the state that they've never really had before.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了他们在该州前所未有的政治扩展可能性。

sentences.en: And then you also had an administration that kept putting race and racial progress at the forefront of its priorities.
sentences.zh: 然后，你还有一个将种族和种族进步置于其优先事项最前沿的政府。

sentences.en: Governor Ralph Northam signed into law sweeping police reform bills this week that will also expand the grounds to decertify officers who commit misconduct,
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·诺瑟姆州长本周签署了一项重大的警察改革法案，该法案还将扩大吊销违纪警员资格的理由，

sentences.en: limit the use of neck restraints, and standardized training requirements.
sentences.zh: 限制使用颈部束缚，并使培训要求标准化。

sentences.en: And Governor Northam got on board with a movement to remove a number of Confederate statues and monuments.
sentences.zh: 诺瑟姆州长还加入了一场旨在移除多座邦联雕像和纪念碑的运动。

sentences.en: Generations ago, Virginia made the decision not to celebrate unity, but to honor the cause of division.
sentences.zh: 几代人以前，弗吉尼亚做出的决定不是庆祝团结，而是为了纪念分裂的事业。

sentences.en: Symbols matter, too.
sentences.zh: 象征意义也很重要。

sentences.en: And Virginia has never been willing to deal with symbols until now.
sentences.zh: 而弗吉尼亚直到现在才愿意去处理这些象征符号。

sentences.en: And I think the last piece for me was the abolition of the death penalty that happened in Virginia, the first state in the South to do so.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说最后一块拼图是弗吉尼亚州废除死刑，这是南部第一个这样做的州。

sentences.en: When one looks at the history, close to 1,400 individuals have been executed.
sentences.zh: 回看历史，有近1400名个人被执行死刑。

sentences.en: The great majority of those individuals were African-American.
sentences.zh: 其中绝大多数都是非裔美国人。

sentences.en: We've executed more people than any other state.
sentences.zh: 我们处决的人比其他任何州都多。

sentences.en: And this is our time to right that wrong.
sentences.zh: 现在是我们纠正这个错误的时候了。

sentences.en: He was someone who was elected not really as a progressive, but as a kind of tried and true Southern, kind of more conservative Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他当选时并非作为一个真正的进步派，而是一个久经考验、根正苗红的南方保守派民主党人。

sentences.en: And he hadn't really leaned into issues of race and identity before 2019.
sentences.zh: 在2019年之前，他并没有真正倾向于种族和身份认同等议题。

sentences.en: And so it was kind of forefront on my mind that after the inauguration and the national elections were over,
sentences.zh: 因此我脑海中浮现的一个想法是，在就职典礼和全国大选结束后，

sentences.en: that it could be a good time to check in with the Northam scandal of 2019.
sentences.zh: 这或许是一个回顾2019年诺瑟姆丑闻的好时机。

sentences.en: How did it change this person who clearly was thought to be, you know, politically dead?
sentences.zh: 这件事是如何改变这个被认为在政治上已经“死”了的人的？

sentences.en: So I went to Virginia and I talked to the governor in his office.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了弗吉尼亚，在办公室里采访了州长。

sentences.en: So instead, what does he say?
sentences.zh: 那么相反，他是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Just kind of initially as a fact-checking thing, I wanted to make sure it's, you know, as you said at the time,
sentences.zh: 最初出于核实事实的目的，我想确保，正如你当时所说的那样，

sentences.en: you still don't recall being either one of the folks on that picture.
sentences.zh: 你仍然记不清自己是否是那张照片里的某个人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: In the interview, the governor reiterates that he does not believe that he is either man in the racist photograph on his yearbook page,
sentences.zh: 在采访中，州长重申他认为自己不是毕业纪念册上那张种族主义照片中的任何一个人，

sentences.en: but that he did wear blackface in a previous incident at a party around the same time.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在大约同一时期的某个聚会上，在之前的另一次事件中把脸涂黑过。

sentences.en: He also states that his main goal after the news broke was to convince his black staff to stick by him.
sentences.zh: 他还表示，消息曝光后他的主要目标是说服他的黑人幕僚继续支持他。

sentences.en: And also he made a pitch to elected officials across the state, particularly the black elected officials, that if they stuck by him,
sentences.zh: 他还向全州的民选官员，特别是黑人民选官员抛出橄榄枝，如果他们支持他，

sentences.en: he would show that he's a changed man and those new priorities will be reflected in his administration.
sentences.zh: 他将证明自己是一个脱胎换骨的人，这些新的优先事项将在他的政府中得到体现。

sentences.en: I said that, you know, I understand what's going on, I know why these people are hurting, and I'm committed to listening and learning and then having the pulpit, if you will,
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，我理解发生了什么，我知道为什么这些人感到痛苦，我致力于倾听、学习，然后利用这个平台——如果你愿意这么说的话——

sentences.en: to really make some significant changes.
sentences.zh: 来真正做出一些重大的改变。

sentences.en: And so that's really the approach that I took.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我采取的方法。

sentences.en: So I never, you know, I was having people, as you may remember, that were really leaning on me to, you know, I needed to resign.
sentences.zh: 因此我从来没有，你知道的，正如你可能记得的那样，当时有人向我施加很大压力，认为我需要辞职。

sentences.en: And I said, I can do more good for people and more good for Virginia.
sentences.zh: 而我说，我可以为人民做更多的好事，为弗吉尼亚做更多的好事。

sentences.en: People will stick with me.
sentences.zh: 人们会支持我的。

sentences.en: And Ralph Northam's telling the way that the scandal changed him starts on the inside.
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·诺瑟姆讲述丑闻如何改变他时，是从内心深处开始的。

sentences.en: That's a moment of embarrassment caused personal growth that then was reflected in his administration's priorities.
sentences.zh: 那是一个由尴尬时刻引发的个人成长，随后体现在他政府的优先工作上。

sentences.en: One of my proudest moments was being at Greensville Correctional Center and signing legislation to get rid of the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 我最骄傲的时刻之一是身处格林斯维尔惩教中心，签署旨在废除死刑的立法。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at the history of that, and it's another example of if what happened in February hadn't happened,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你回顾那段历史，这也是另一个例子：如果2月份没有发生那样的事，

sentences.en: I'm not sure if my eyes would have been opened to the point where I went back and looked at the history and how many people of color had been executed and why, you know,
sentences.zh: 我不敢确定我的双眼是否会被唤醒到这种程度，以至于我去回溯历史，看看有多少有色人种被处决，以及为什么，你知道的，

sentences.en: capital punishment was being used.
sentences.zh: 死刑当时是如何被使用的。

sentences.en: And I mean, we could go through example after example, whether it be access to health care, access to education or access to business opportunities or voting that are all just,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们可以举出一个又一个例子，无论是获得医疗保健的机会、接受教育的机会、还是获得商业机会或投票的机会，全都是，

sentences.en: you know, just full of racism and oppression that they were, I guess, in front of my eyes, but my brain didn't know about them at the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，充满了种族主义和压迫，它们当时就摆在我眼前，但我当时的脑子并不知道这些。

sentences.en: And so that's why I'm a much better person now than I was.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么现在的我比以前要好得多。

sentences.en: And that eyes and brain, mind mill, February 19th brought together.
sentences.zh: 而2月19日让我的双眼和大脑、心灵融为一体。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: But I wanted to ask him, how much of this is also about politics?
sentences.zh: 但我想问他，这其中又有多少是出于政治考量？

sentences.en: How much of this is about him repaying a black community that's stuck by him at his darkest time?
sentences.zh: 这其中有多少是他为了报答在他最黑暗时刻仍然支持他的黑人群体？

sentences.en: Someone told me today that the policy has paid back the debt.
sentences.zh: 今天有人对我说，政策已经偿还了这笔债务。

sentences.en: What do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: You know, I'm not one to, I don't go around taking credit for things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是那种人，我不会到处去为事情邀功。

sentences.en: I think the good policy that has come from all this has been a team effort.
sentences.zh: 我认为由此产生的好政策是团队合作的结果。

sentences.en: A lot of these things would not have happened if we didn't have the majority in the House and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有在众议院和参议院占据多数席位，许多事情是不会发生的。

sentences.en: And so, well, I don't want to take all the credit for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然我不想把所有的功劳都归功于自己，

sentences.en: But this has been a team effort.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一次团队的努力。

sentences.en: And it's been an effort where, again, I've sat down with people and said, these are some things that we can do.
sentences.zh: 这也是一次我再次与人们坐在一起，并说道“这些是我们能够做到的一些事情”的努力。

sentences.en: And it's all about time and opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这一切都关乎时机和机遇。

sentences.en: When he talks to the people around him, they make very clear that he has taken this period of growth very seriously.
sentences.zh: 当他与身边的人交谈时，他们明确表示他非常严肃地对待这段成长时期。

sentences.en: That he has really made it his mission to learn about what he says he was ignorant of, the history of race and racism before this scandal.
sentences.zh: 他真的把了解自己曾经无知的事物——即这场丑闻之前的种族与种族主义历史——当作了自己的使命。

sentences.en: But for a lot of Black leaders in the state, whether they were elected officials or whether they were activists, they're frankly unconcerned with how true his growth personally is.
sentences.zh: 但对于该州的许多黑人领袖来说，无论是民选官员还是活动人士，他们坦言并不关心他的个人成长究竟有几分真实。

sentences.en: This was a moment of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满机遇的时刻。

sentences.en: There was a window in which the governor was asking you, what can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 当时正值一个窗口期，州长在问你：我能为你做些什么？

sentences.en: And they decided that they were going to seize on that.
sentences.zh: 而他们决定抓住这个机会。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Ested, you said some of the Black leaders in Virginia saw this scandal with Northam as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 那么，阿斯特德，你提到弗吉尼亚州的一些黑人领袖将诺瑟姆的这场丑闻视为一个机遇。

sentences.en: What did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: One of the people I talked to about that was one of his campaign co-chairs from when Ralph Northam originally ran for governor.
sentences.zh: 我为此交谈过的人之一，是拉尔夫·诺瑟姆最初竞选州长时的竞选联合主席之一。

sentences.en: And her name is Marcia Price.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫玛西娅·普赖斯。

sentences.en: I am a delegate for the 95th District, which is parts of Newport, Newver, Hampton, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我是第95选区的代表，该选区涵盖弗吉尼亚州纽波特纽斯和汉普顿的部分地区。

sentences.en: She's a member of what is functionally the House of Representatives for the state of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 她是弗吉尼亚州实质上的众议院议员。

sentences.en: And she had really put her credibility on the line to help get Northam elected in what was a competitive Democratic primary.
sentences.zh: 在一场竞争激烈的民主党初选中，她确实拿出了自己的信誉来帮助诺瑟姆当选。

sentences.en: So she was going across the state with him kind of as a liaison to Black voters and community leaders back when he was initially running to be governor.
sentences.zh: 因此，早在诺瑟姆最初竞选州长时，她就作为黑人选民和社区领袖的联络人，随他走遍了全州。

sentences.en: So we had gone into intimate spaces within, you know, my network when we were running.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们参选时，我们已经进入了我人脉网络内部的私密空间。

sentences.en: And she said that when she found out about the photo scandal, she was crushed.
sentences.zh: 她说，当她发现照片丑闻时，她崩溃了。

sentences.en: The moment where he broke, it hurt.
sentences.zh: 他决裂的那一刻，真的很痛。

sentences.en: It hurt like hell.
sentences.zh: 痛彻心扉。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: She has this initial reaction.
sentences.zh: 她最初有这样的反应。

sentences.en: Then what does she do?
sentences.zh: 然后她做了什么？

sentences.en: When she went home to her district as this was going on,
sentences.zh: 当事件发酵、她回到自己的选区时，

sentences.en: it became very clear to her that the feeling among the Black Virginians she was representing was way more diverse and nuanced than the feelings that were happening on the national level.
sentences.zh: 她变得非常清楚，她所代表的弗吉尼亚黑人群体中的感受，要比全国层面的情绪更加多元和微妙。

sentences.en: That weekend and several weekends after people were coming up to me and making sure I knew how they felt on either side, you know, whether he should,
sentences.zh: 那个周末以及之后的几个周末，人们纷纷走过来，确保我知道他们各自的立场——无论是关于他应该，

sentences.en: whether we should push him out, you know, or, or y'all leave that man alone and take this as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我们是否应该把他赶下台，还是说“哎呀，别管那个人了，抓住这个机会吧”。

sentences.en: And so, well, that was back then, who is he now?
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，那是过去，现在的他又是什么样的人？

sentences.en: It was not excusing bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 这并不是在为不良行为开脱。

sentences.en: It was an understanding on their part, not speaking for myself, but understanding on their part,
sentences.zh: 这是他们的一种理解——我不是在替我自己发言，而是理解他们的看法——

sentences.en: that if you cut ties with every white man that has done something that was questionable or that you didn't agree with, we couldn't get business done.
sentences.zh: 如果你与每一个做过可疑事情或你不同意的白人男子断绝关系，我们就没法办成任何事了。

sentences.en: You have to remember that we're talking about Black people who have lived in the South for a long time.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，我们讨论的是在南方生活了很久的黑人群体。

sentences.en: And that is a different type of racial landscape.
sentences.zh: 那是另一种截然不同的种族地貌。

sentences.en: So while there are certainly people who saw that photo and immediately wanted Northam to resign,
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然确实有人看到那张照片后立刻希望诺瑟姆辞职，

sentences.en: there are also people who have already kind of baked in the racism of white Americans in the South and didn't find it particularly surprising.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人，他们对南方白人美国人根深蒂固的种族主义早已见怪不怪，并不觉得这有什么特别令人惊讶的。

sentences.en: And some who didn't find it particularly invalidating.
sentences.zh: 也有人觉得这并没有彻底否定什么。

sentences.en: I'm a 10th generation resident born in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我是出生在弗吉尼亚州的第十代居民。

sentences.en: This is where it started in some senses, you know, and it is not surprising that it took something huge for someone to realize I have privilege.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，一切就是从这里开始的，你知道的，所以出现这样一件大事才让某个人意识到我有特权，这并不让人意外。

sentences.en: I need to learn more because that's the system that we're up against on all of this.
sentences.zh: 我需要了解更多，因为这就是我们面对的整个系统。

sentences.en: You can see how it's important that all of these things happened at once.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，所有这些事情同时发生是多么重要。

sentences.en: You had the additional scandals for his would-be successors.
sentences.zh: 你还要应付他那些潜在继任者的其他丑闻。

sentences.en: You had Northam pitching, what can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 诺瑟姆当时抛出橄榄枝问：我能为你做些什么？

sentences.en: And you had her listening to her constituents who were giving a more mixed and nuanced reception than the national pressure.
sentences.zh: 而她则在倾听选民的声音，与全国范围内的压力相比，选民们的反应更加复杂和微妙。

sentences.en: And so what she says is that it became clear to her that the most strategic decision, the one that had the biggest upside for her constituents,
sentences.zh: 所以她说得很清楚，对她而言最具有战略意义、对选民最有利的决定，

sentences.en: is to take the governor up on that offer and to really try to use their sense of collective power as Black elected officials and as the communities that stood by him in this moment to say,
sentences.zh: 就是接受州长的提议，真正尝试利用他们作为黑人民选官员以及在此时支持他的社区的集体力量去表态：

sentences.en: OK, if we do that, we're going to expect things down the line.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我们这样做，我们以后就会有所期待。

sentences.en: If I shut down and didn't seize the opportunity to have further conversations and to work toward legislation that my district needed, that I wasn't doing my job.
sentences.zh: 如果我闭门不见，没有抓住机会进行进一步对话，也没有去争取我选区需要的立法，那就是我失职。

sentences.en: It was strategic.
sentences.zh: 这是出于战略考量。

sentences.en: If he's in a position now for us to get some things done, then y'all get some things done.
sentences.zh: 如果他现在有能力让我们办成一些事，那你们就去把事情办成。

sentences.en: I mean, it is kind of a sad commentary that it would take a moment of racism to push what is a loyal group of Democratic voters to the top of the priority liSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为一个忠诚的民主党选民群体，竟然需要经历一桩种族主义丑闻才能被推到优先级名单的顶端，这实在是一个可悲的现象。

sentences.en: But basically, that's the decision they come to, is to say, OK, he's pitching this specifically around policy, and we're sick of being not taken seriously at that table.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，他们做出的决定就是：好吧，他既然专门围绕政策抛出橄榄枝，而我们又厌倦了在谈判桌上不被认真对待。

sentences.en: So maybe in this moment, there's an alignment of values that doesn't often exist, even within the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 那么也许在这个时刻，会出现一种价值观上的一致，这种一致在民主党内部往往也是不存在的。

sentences.en: I definitely can say I feel more listened to by the administration since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我绝对可以说，自2019年以来，我感到本届政府更加倾听我们的声音了。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's by happenstance, but I also think that that's really important for my district.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是偶然发生的，而且我也认为这对于我的选区来说真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And then you look at what got done.
sentences.zh: 然后你看看取得了什么成果。

sentences.en: It's things the Black Caucus has been fighting for.
sentences.zh: 这些都是黑人党团一直以来在争取的事情。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And so I don't think that it should be taken as just we let it go or everything was just all fine.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这不应该被视作我们就此放手，或者一切都好得很。

sentences.en: It was we had business, and we had to do the business, or else we wouldn't have been living up to our end of the bargain as elected officials.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的：我们有公务在身，必须把公务处理好，否则我们就没有兑现作为民选官员应尽的职责。

sentences.en: And just to know that I have a governor who is listening when I talk about, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且只要知道当我谈论某些事情时，州长是在倾听的，

sentences.en: the Voting Rights Act of Virginia and why it's still needed in 2021 and why Virginia can be in a different position and trajectory on voting rights than your Georgia or Texas or,
sentences.zh: 比如弗吉尼亚州的《选举权法》，以及为什么在2021年它仍然必不可少，为什么弗吉尼亚州在选举权方面能够拥有与佐治亚州、得克萨斯州或，

sentences.en: you know, Arizona, that is not real work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，亚利桑那州不同的立场和发展轨迹，这才是真正的工作。

sentences.en: Boots on the ground, real work with the advocates and legislators who stayed at the table because they knew they couldn't leave.
sentences.zh: 脚踏实地、与那些坚守阵地因为知道不能离开的倡导者和立法者一起开展的真正工作。

sentences.en: You know, she's someone who's had a long relationship with the governor, obviously from his campaign all the way through, and then had the moment of hurt when the scandal came out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她与州长有着长期的关系，显然从竞选一路走来，然后在丑闻曝光时也经历过心碎的时刻。

sentences.en: I was wondering how she viewed him now, even if she wasn't surprised or she expects little when it comes to white Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我想知道她现在是怎么看他的，即便她并不感到惊讶，或者对白人民主党人本来就抱持很低的期待。

sentences.en: After what he's done, does she consider him an ally to Black communities?
sentences.zh: 在他做了那些事之后，她还认为他是黑人社区的盟友吗？

sentences.en: You mentioned you don't call everyone an ally.
sentences.zh: 你提到过你不会把所有人称为盟友。

sentences.en: Is Ralph Northam one in your book?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，拉尔夫·诺瑟姆算是一个吗？

sentences.en: And instead, what did you make of her answer?
sentences.zh: 对于她的回答，你又是怎么看的呢？

sentences.en: I think in its core, she shows the real pragmatism that Black voters are forced to think about in a two-party democratic system.
sentences.zh: 我认为从根本上说，她展现了黑人在两党民主制度下不得不去考量的现实主义。

sentences.en: That the choices have often, for Black people in America, been between bad and worse.
sentences.zh: 对于美国的黑人来说，选择往往是在糟糕和更糟糕之间做出的。

sentences.en: And for communities that have often not had the system work for them, to cancel everyone who has done a racist thing in the past is an ability they do not have.
sentences.zh: 对于那些体制往往无法为他们服务的社区来说，一棍子打死所有过去做过种族主义事情的人，是他们做不到的。

sentences.en: And so when you ask her if he's an ally, I think her response shows how meaningless, really, that word is for the political system.
sentences.zh: 所以当你问她他是否是盟友时，我认为她的回答表明了这个词对政治体制而言实际上是多么毫无意义。

sentences.en: She doesn't need him to be an ally.
sentences.zh: 她不需要他成为盟友。

sentences.en: And frankly, it's not important if he's an ally.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，他是不是盟友也并不重要。

sentences.en: What is important for her is that he reflects the things that she believes her community needs.
sentences.zh: 对她而言重要的是，他所体现的东西反映了她认为自己社区所需要的事物。

sentences.en: And to me, that is the Black political experience in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这就是黑人政治经历的缩影。

sentences.en: It's not about being my friend.
sentences.zh: 这无关乎做我的朋友。

sentences.en: It's about delivering on stuff.
sentences.zh: 这关乎把事情办成。

sentences.en: There have been few friends for Black people in the scope of American politics.
sentences.zh: 在美利坚政治的宏大叙事中，黑人的朋友寥寥无几。

sentences.en: It is about who has been willing to be a vessel for that progress.
sentences.zh: 关键在于谁愿意成为实现这种进步的载体。

sentences.en: And that has come in many, many forms throughout our history.
sentences.zh: 在我们的历史上，这种载体曾以各种各样、形形色色的面貌出现。

sentences.en: People who are open racists, people who are segregationists, people who are slave owners.
sentences.zh: 公开的种族主义者、隔离主义者、奴隶主。

sentences.en: People, you know, that has been true kind of throughout.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，各种人都有，这种现象贯穿始终。

sentences.en: And I think that that is particularly top of mind for Black elected officials in the South who have known that directly and have known to navigate that throughout their careers.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于南方的黑人民选官员来说尤为重要，他们对此有着直接的体会，并在其整个职业生涯中深知如何应对。

sentences.en: Ested, thank you.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特德，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Now, I told President Putin my agenda is not against Russia or anyone else.
sentences.zh: 现在，我告诉普京总统，我的议程不是针对俄罗斯或任何人。

sentences.en: It's for the American people.
sentences.zh: 它是为了美国人民。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, following their first in-person meeting, President Biden and the president of Russia, Vladimir Putin, described their encounter as constructive and positive.
sentences.zh: 周三，在进行了首次面对面会晤后，拜登总统与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京将他们的会面描述为建设性和积极的。

sentences.en: But during back-to-back news conferences with reporters in Geneva,
sentences.zh: 但在日内瓦与记者的密集新闻发布会上，

sentences.en: it became clear that the leaders remained deeply at odds over issues like human rights and online meddling in elections, which Biden told Putin must stop.
sentences.zh: 情况变得明朗起来，两国领导人在人权和网络干预选举等问题上依然存在严重分歧，拜登告诉普京这些行为必须停止。

sentences.en: I made it clear that we will not tolerate attempts to violate our democratic sovereignty or to stabilize our democratic elections, and we would respond.
sentences.zh: 我明确表示，我们不会容忍任何试图破坏我们民主主权或破坏我们民主选举稳定的行为，我们将作出回应。

sentences.en: Biden said he had warned Putin not to bring any harm to Alexei Navalny, the Russian opposition leader jailed by Putin's government.
sentences.zh: 拜登表示，他曾警告普京不要对阿列克谢·纳瓦尔尼造成任何伤害，这位俄罗斯反对派领导人目前正被普京政府关押。

sentences.en: The bottom line is I told President Putin that we need to have some basic rules of the road that we can all abide by.
sentences.zh: 最根本的是，我告诉普京总统，我们需要有一些大家都能够遵守的基本规则。

sentences.en: Asked about Navalny during his own news conference, Putin countered that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在自己的新闻发布会上被问及纳瓦尔尼时，普京反驳称，美国

sentences.en: was silencing its own dissidents by arresting those who stormed the Capitol on January 6th and said that Russia wanted to avoid the kind of political violence that had occurred in the United States during protests over policing last summer.
sentences.zh: 通过逮捕1月6日冲击国会大厦的人来压制自己的异见人士，并表示俄罗斯希望避免像去年夏天美国在抗议执法期间发生的那种政治暴力。

sentences.en: What we saw was disorder destruction, violations of the law, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是混乱、破坏、违法行为等等。

sentences.en: We feel sympathy for the United States of America, but we don't want that to happen on our territory, and we're doing our utmost in order to not allow it to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们对美利坚合众国感同身受，但我们不希望这种事在我们的领土上发生，我们正在尽最大努力不让它发生。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Eric Krupke, Diana Nguyen, and Luke Vanderplug.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由埃里克·克鲁普克、黛安娜·阮和卢克·范德普鲁格制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Dave Shaw and Lisa Chow, contains original music by Dan Powell and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由戴夫·肖和莉萨·乔伊编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛扎诺的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bovaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为我们带来假期招待客人的准备工作。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要黑暗环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到不省人事才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require, because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
